title: Reconcile workspace manifests and package ownership

acceptanceResults.criterion: One root install resolves every production workspace dependency locally.
acceptanceResults.evidence: bun install registers all 19 workspace members with no registry fetch for an internal name, and findUnresolvedWorkspaceDependencies reports zero. Archify's ajv, parse5, saxes and simple-icons were translated from devDependencies to dependencies because the renderers import them at runtime; the fast-uri 3.1.5 override was preserved.

acceptanceResults.criterion: Duplicate package names, hidden npm fallbacks and accidental published upstream package substitution fail validation.
acceptanceResults.evidence: validateWorkspace detects all three, each asserted with a fixture. The inherited packages/diagram-engine/package-lock.json was a real second package-manager root inside a bun workspace member and was relocated to docs/upstream/archify/. An internal dependency declared with a registry range instead of workspace:* is reported as registry-substitution, which is the exact mechanism by which a published upstream package could silently replace an owned one.

acceptanceResults.criterion: Native HyperFrames packages remain available; no package is removed merely because the diagram slice does not use it.
acceptanceResults.evidence: All 14 inherited packages remain registered and are asserted by name, including aws-lambda, gcp-cloud-run, sdk-playground and shader-transitions, none of which the diagram slice touches.

notPerformed: The @hyperframes scope was deliberately retained. Contract C11 requires a scope rename to update code, lockfile, exports, build scripts, skills and distribution tests atomically, which is its own ticket.
project-model and diagram-motion carry manifests and contract declarations only. Their implementations are E03 (AFM-017) and E05 (AFM-039).
